provenance.statement: Every figure below is a conservative class value compiled from free, public sources, rounded in the defender's disfavor (the attacker is assumed fast and cheap). No measurement precision is claimed: these are order-of-magnitude anchors for the bench's dollar comparison, refreshed by hand, and the bench prints this file's as_of beside every derived dollar figure. The declared abuse values are not free-hand policy guesses: they are calibrated from the bench's own measured attacker costs through the margin rule in economics.calibration.
source_classes: public GPU cracking benchmark indices (hashcat-class raw sha256 figures)
public cloud spot pricing indices (consumer GPU and one CPU core rental)
provenance.refresh_note: Refresh by re-checking the source classes above, re-running the D3.3 campaign on the release bench host, and recalibrating the declared values through economics.calibration; bump as_of. Stale entries must be replaced, never silently kept. The bench flags any as_of older than a year in its output.
provenance.honesty: argon2id and rsw deliberately carry no attacker-rate entries. Published GPU argon2id figures swing with the memory cost and vendor, so one number would fabricate precision; rsw squaring is inherently sequential and no hardware class buys a parallel speedup. For those rungs the bench reports the native measurement and prints insufficient-reference-data verdicts instead of guessing. Where the cheapest tabled attacker still undercuts a declared value, raw PoW cannot price that value and the documented answer is the disposition escalation (a step_up or deny minimum), not a bigger number.

economics.provenance: public cloud spot pricing indices, one core-hour, rounded down in the defender's disfavor

calibration.rule: declared_abuse_value is an independent per-account stake (public resale reporting). anchor_usd_per_1000 is the measured attacker cost and is the ceiling: a declared stake above the ceiling means PoW cannot price the scope and the disposition must escalate.
calibration.note: The previous rule (declared = anchor/10) was circular: cost > cost/10 always held, so D3.3 could never fail.

economics.statement: Every figure below is a conservative class value compiled from free, public sources, rounded in the defender's disfavor.
